title: Two-vertex cuts and a Lorentzian obstruction for bistable bipartite graphs
scope: For every integer k>=2 and every finite connected simple bipartite graph F with parts L,R of size k whose only maximum independent sets are L and R, set A=[[0,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,1]], f=Z_(F,A) with the unnormalized labeled-assignment convention in problem.md, beta=(k-1,k-1,0), and c=[x1^(k-1)x2^(k-1)x3^2]f. For distinct u,v let q(u,v) be the number of connected components of F-{u,v}, including isolated vertices; let s count unordered pairs within L or within R for which q(u,v)>1. Then c=sum_(u in L,v in R)2^q(u,v)+2s and Hessian(partial^beta f)=2(k!)^2 [[0,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,c/k^2]]. In particular c>=2k^2, with equality exactly when F has no two-vertex cut. Such F is 2-connected. The selected Hessian has two positive eigenvalues exactly when F is not 3-connected, proving that f is not Lorentzian in that case; A is admissible with spectrum -1,1-sqrt(2),1+sqrt(2). If F is 3-connected this Hessian has one positive, one negative, and one zero eigenvalue, without any assertion that f itself is Lorentzian. Corollaries: c=6k(k-1) for C_(2k), k>=2; c=2k^2 for K_(k,k), k>=3; c=12 for K_(2,2)=C4. The original universal connected-clique characterization remains unresolved.

title: A counterexample to distributivity of fixed pinnacle-order fibers
scope: Let P_5((5)) be all permutations of [5] whose complete left-to-right list of interior pinnacle values is exactly (5), with endpoints excluded from peaks. Order this fiber by coordinatewise comparison of I_v(pi), the number of values smaller than v to the right of v. This nonempty induced poset is not a distributive lattice. An exact witness consists of e=12354, b=12534, a=13524, c=13452, d=13542. All five lie in the fiber, and their meets and joins computed among every element of the fiber satisfy b join c=d, a meet d=a, a meet b=b, a meet c=e, b join e=b, with a different from b. Thus a meet (b join c) differs from (a meet b) join (a meet c). This disproves the universal assertion asked in Liang--Sagan Question 8.6(a) in the published version, equivalently Question 8.7(a) of arXiv:2408.02782v1, including its explicitly qualified nonempty-fiber version. No assertion about counting part (b), minimality in n, or a classification of other fibers is submitted.

title: An Ehrhart–word identity for arbor polytopes
scope: For every integer n>=1, every partition of [n] into nonempty blocks B_v, and every rooted tree tau on those blocks, let D_v be the union of descendant blocks including B_v and N_v=|D_v|. Set Q_tau={x in R^n: x_i>=0 for all i and sum_{i in D_v} x_i<=N_v for every v}. Let W_tau be all length-n words over [n] with at least N_v occurrences of letters from D_v for every v, and des(w)=|{j:1<=j<n, w_j>w_{j+1}}|. With sum_{m>=0}|m Q_tau intersect Z^n| t^m=h*(Q_tau,t)/(1-t)^(n+1), one has h*(Q_tau,t)=sum_{w in W_tau} t^(n-1-des(w)). Equivalently, for every integer m>=0, |m Q_tau intersect Z^n|=sum_{a in A_tau} product_{i=1}^n binom(m+1,a_i), where A_tau={a in Z_{≥0}^n:sum_i a_i=n and sum_{i in D_v} a_i>=N_v for every v}, and binom(m+1,a_i)=0 when a_i>m+1. No restriction on block labels, sizes, depth, or branching is imposed.
